candidates.folded:
Understanding Retention Policies in Northgate Vault

A ~3:entionret policy determines how long Northgate Vault keeps a ~2:cumentdo before it becomes
eligible for permanent deletion. Every ~2:cumentdo inherits exactly one ~3:entionret policy, and that
policy is resolved at the moment the ~2:cumentdo is created. Changing a policy later affects only
~2:cumentsdo created after the change; it never retroactively alters the disposition date of a
~2:cumentdo that already exists. This behaviour is deliberate, because retroactive changes would
make it impossible to prove to an auditor what the disposition ~1:chedules was at any given point
in the past.

Policies are evaluated in a fixed order. The system first looks for a policy attached directly to
the ~2:cumentdo. If none exists, it looks for a policy attached to the folder that contains the
~2:cumentdo, then to that folder's parent, and so on up to the ~6:aceworksp root. If no policy is found
anywhere on that path, the ~6:aceworksp default applies. The ~6:aceworksp default cannot be removed,
only changed, which guarantees that every ~2:cumentdo always resolves to some policy.

There are three kinds of disposition. Soft deletion moves the ~2:cumentdo to a recycle bin where it
remains visible to administrators for a further thirty days. Hard deletion removes the ~2:cumentdo
content but keeps an immutable audit stub recording that a ~2:cumentdo existed, who created it, and
when it was disposed. Purge removes everything, including the audit stub, and is only available
to workspaces operating under a legal regime that requires it; most customers should never enable
purge, because it destroys the evidence that the ~3:entionret policy was followed.

A legal hold suspends all disposition for the ~2:cumentsdo it covers. Holds take precedence over
every policy, including purge, and they cannot be overridden by an administrator. Only a user with
the Legal Hold Officer role may place or release a hold, and every placement and release is
written to the audit log with the reason supplied by that user. When a hold is released, the
affected ~2:cumentsdo return to their normal ~1:chedules; if their disposition date has already passed,
they become eligible immediately and will be processed in the next nightly sweep.

The nightly sweep runs at 02:00 in the ~6:aceworksp's configured timezone. It processes ~2:cumentsdo in
creation order, oldest first, and stops after four hours regardless of how much work remains.
Anything not processed is picked up by the next sweep. Because the sweep is time-bounded rather
than work-bounded, a ~6:aceworksp with a very large backlog may take several nights to catch up, and
administrators sometimes mistake this for a failure. The sweep report, available under Reports and
Audit, shows exactly how many ~2:cumentsdo were considered, how many were disposed, and how many
remained in the queue when the sweep stopped.

Two questions come up repeatedly in support tickets. The first is why a ~2:cumentdo with an expired
disposition date is still visible. Almost always the answer is either an active legal hold or a
backlogged sweep, both of which the sweep report will show. The second is whether a ~3:entionret
policy can be shortened. It can, but only for future ~2:cumentsdo, and the interface deliberately
makes this awkward in order to prevent an administrator from accidentally believing that existing
~2:cumentsdo have been reshuffled onto the shorter ~1:chedules.
